rootCause.details: The repaired revision, like the accepted fix, synchronizes the Ora interval only while assigning a custom spinner object and only when that object has an interval value other than undefined.

behavior.details: A direct probe produced identical repaired and accepted results: constructor override 300, positive custom interval 200, zero custom interval 0, omitted custom interval preserving 444, named-spinner assignment preserving 333, and named-spinner construction using 80.

tests.details: The repaired tests cover positive, zero, omitted, constructor-precedence, and named-spinner cases. Independent QA reported all 26 AVA tests and TSD passing; the auditor also ran the direct state probe against both exact revisions.

scope.details: The change is confined to custom-object spinner assignment plus focused regression tests. It removes the first attempt's unintended named-spinner behavior change.

simplicity.details: The explicit `spinner.interval !== undefined` guard is small, readable, and behaviorally equivalent to the accepted correction.

regressions.details: The accepted counterexamples that failed the first attempt now pass: interval 0 is retained and assigning a built-in spinner name no longer overwrites the instance interval. No regression was observed in the practical suite.

limitations: The direct comparison used deterministic public state probes rather than rerunning the accepted revision's complete historical CI matrix.
XO reported an environment/version warning during independent QA; AVA and TSD passed, and the warning did not affect the compared behavior.
The initial failed audit and QA false positive remain unchanged under evidence/attempt-1 and are retained in the historical count.
